LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING: PUNCTUATION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation, part of Strand 7 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Which punctuation marks do you know? 2. Why do we punctuate sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a short text and identify punctuation marks used collaboratively with peers,

2. use commas to s

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a short text and identify punctuation marks used collaboratively with peers,
2. use commas to s

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of Writing: Punctuation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner takes up assigned duties and roles in creating posters with sentences using

correct use of punctuation marks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively when picking out

magazines, reading and identifying punctuation marks used.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the concept of correct punctuation in writing in all learning areas particularly in Kiswahili.
